references.text: The priest takes a handful of the flour as a memorial portion (אַזְכָּרָה) and burns it on the altar, following the same procedure described here.
The memorial portion (אַזְכָּרָה) is taken from the grain offering and burned on the altar as a food offering to the Lord.
The priest burns the memorial portion as a food offering to the Lord, parallel to the sin offering procedure in 5:12.
Describes the priest's handling of the grain offering and the memorial portion that is burned on the altar.
Previous verses explaining the context: the sin offering of flour without oil or frankincense for the poor.
Following verses explain that the priest makes atonement for the sin, and the remainder of the flour belongs to the priest as with the grain offering.
A food offering (אִשֵּׁה) to the Lord is burned on the altar; the same terminology is used for this offering.
The priest burns the memorial portion on the altar, following the same procedure of קָמַץ (taking a handful).
